reviews.reasoning: Numbering re-derived through ps_lib.web_to_mt rather than taken from the row: Ps 77 is shift+1, so web:Ps.77.0 = oshb:Ps.77.1 and web:Ps.77.1-20 = oshb:Ps.77.2-21; the 4 refs here are arithmetically correct and the title pseudo-ref carries the owner-ruled form. All 5 Hebrew runs in the row collate at byte tier against the verse each cites (5 of 5). The K/Q disclosure at oshb:Ps.77.1 agrees with the inventory, which records 3 K/Q verses in this psalm: oshb:Ps.77.1, oshb:Ps.77.12, oshb:Ps.77.20 (unit = verses). The back seam holds on tier-1 grounds that do not need selah: across the 3 verses oshb:Ps.77.2-4 (web:Ps.77.1-3) the psalm body carries 0 second-person-masculine-singular tokens, and the earliest one arrives at oshb:Ps.77.5 = web:Ps.77.4 ('אָ֭חַזְתָּ'; unit = tokens), so the addressee shift falls exactly on the seam and the selah at oshb:Ps.77.4 corroborates rather than drives. The device_notes label count re-derives correctly: the labels shared with Psalm 76's title are 3, namely lamnatseach, mizmor and le-Asaph (unit = labels). What fails is the evidence, not the span: the doubled-cry claim is not exhibited by the bytes the row quotes and its tier goes unnamed; the cross-psalm title comparison argues 3 psalms outside the span without refs and puts the ketiv/qere on the wrong side of its own contrast; and the rejected_alternative rejects its rival by citing campaign governance instead of text.

challenges.claim: The row asserts that the 'my voice to God' phrase repeats inside oshb:Ps.77.2, but its quoted bytes carry 1 of 2 occurrences, and the 2 are not byte-equal: the repetition holds at accent_stripped and skeleton tier, a tier the row leaves unnamed.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.77.2 = web:Ps.77.1 (shift+1). The 2 cola are 'קוֹלִ֣י אֶל אֱלֹהִ֣ים' and 'קוֹלִ֥י אֶל אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים'; collating one against the other returns byte False, nfd False, accent_stripped True, skeleton True, because the accents differ (colon A carries U+05A3 on both words, colon B carries U+05A5 and U+059D with U+0597). A skeleton sweep of the verse returns 2 occurrences of 'קולי אל אלהים' (unit = occurrences inside oshb:Ps.77.2), and a repeated-string sweep across oshb:Ps.77.1-21 returns 1 repeated 3-word skeleton string in the psalm, both of whose 2 occurrences sit inside this one verse (unit = strings), so the doubling is real and it is this psalm's sole repetition of that length. The row's quoted Hebrew 'קוֹלִ֣י אֶל אֱלֹהִ֣ים וְאֶצְעָ֑קָה' carries 1 of 2 occurrences at byte tier, while its curly WEB gloss “My cry goes to God! Indeed, I cry to God for help…” (web:Ps.77.1) spans both cola: quote and gloss do not cover the same span, and the repetition the sentence asserts is precisely what the Hebrew leaves out.

challenges.claim: The title comparison argues 3 psalms outside this row's span, 62, 39 and 76, without a dual-cited ref for any of the 3, and hangs the ketiv/qere pair on Psalm 62, whose title has 0 K/Q notes, while contrasting Psalm 39, whose title holds the 1 note that shares the ketiv spelling.
challenges.evidence: K/Q inventory counts: oshb:Ps.77.1 = 1 note, oshb:Ps.39.1 = 1 note, oshb:Ps.62.1 = 0 notes (unit = notes). Bytes: oshb:Ps.77.1 = web:Ps.77.0 reads 'לַמְנַצֵּ֥חַ עַֽל ידיתון יְדוּת֗וּן לְאָסָ֥ף מִזְמֽוֹר'; oshb:Ps.39.1 = web:Ps.39.0 reads 'לַמְנַצֵּ֥חַ לידיתון לִֽידוּת֗וּן מִזְמ֥וֹר לְדָוִֽד', whose ketiv 'לידיתון' carries the same consonantal Yeduthun spelling as Psalm 77's ketiv under a lamed; oshb:Ps.62.1 = web:Ps.62.0 reads 'לַמְנַצֵּ֥חַ עַֽל יְדוּת֗וּן מִזְמ֥וֹר לְדָוִֽד', a pointed 'יְדוּת֗וּן' backed by 0 ketiv notes. The al-Yeduthun label reading is defensible on its own terms, but the sentence makes the ketiv/qere pair its grammatical subject, so the 1 feature Psalm 77's title shares with 39 and not with 62 ends up on the losing side of the contrast the row draws. Separately, neither web:Ps.62.0 = oshb:Ps.62.1, nor web:Ps.39.0 = oshb:Ps.39.1, nor web:Ps.76.0 = oshb:Ps.76.1 appears in boundary_evidence_refs, so 0 of the 3 comparisons is checkable from the row; check_refs_mirror passes it because these mentions hold no verse numeral for the tool to resolve.

challenges.claim: The rejected_alternative dismisses its rival by appeal to campaign governance rather than to text, which is both a register violation and a warrant substitution in prose that ships with the chunk.
challenges.evidence: The field reads, in the row's own wording, 'but the brief's owner ruling treats titled-psalm superscriptions as tier-1 opener evidence'. A shipped chunk row is consumed without that brief, and the standing register rule bars governance narration from row prose outright. The replacement warrant that passes the same test is already in the row's hands: the title at oshb:Ps.77.1 = web:Ps.77.0 carries 4 superscription labels (unit = labels), 3 of them recurring in Psalm 76's title, and the psalm body opens its second-person address at oshb:Ps.77.5 = web:Ps.77.4 after 3 verses that hold 0 such tokens, so the opener's boundary weight argues from the title's own content and the body's addressee profile without naming any ruling.

reviews.reasoning: Refs re-derived: web:Ps.77.3 = oshb:Ps.77.4, web:Ps.77.4 = oshb:Ps.77.5, web:Ps.77.6 = oshb:Ps.77.7, web:Ps.77.7 = oshb:Ps.77.8, web:Ps.77.9 = oshb:Ps.77.10, correct at 5 of 5 under shift+1, and the 2 out-of-span refs are both argued in the prose. The row's 3 Hebrew runs collate at byte tier against oshb:Ps.77.4 and oshb:Ps.77.10, and its curly WEB quotes check verbatim against the source (16 of 16 across the cluster carry no flag). This row has the best-anchored front seam in the cluster, and I re-derived it rather than accepting it: across the 3 verses oshb:Ps.77.2-4 the body holds 0 second-person-masculine-singular tokens, the earliest attested at oshb:Ps.77.5 = web:Ps.77.4 in the perfect 'אָ֭חַזְתָּ' (unit = tokens), so the addressee shift lands exactly on the seam and the selah at oshb:Ps.77.4 does corroboration only, which is all the evidence rules permit it. The back seam is equally defensible from the Hebrew: an interrogative he opens 3 consecutive verses at oshb:Ps.77.8, oshb:Ps.77.9 and oshb:Ps.77.10 = web:Ps.77.7-9 (unit = verses) and the series stops there. The 3 K/Q verses of this psalm all fall outside oshb:Ps.77.5-10, so nothing was owed on disclosure, and selah is disclosed symmetrically at both seams. Observation, not a defect: the discourse-frame signal cites where WEB's quotation marks open and close rather than the interrogative he opening each of those 3 verses in the Hebrew. The punctuation statement is true of the WEB text and the row's independent anchor at web:Ps.77.6 does not rest on it, so I do not file it, but the Hebrew signal is the stronger of the two and it sits in-span and free.

Refs re-derived and correct at 7 of 7, including the 2 out-of-span pairs the rejected_alternative argues (web:Ps.77.7 = oshb:Ps.77.8, web:Ps.77.8 = oshb:Ps.77.9). All 4 Hebrew runs collate at byte tier. The series ordinal byte-settles before anything is argued from it: Ps 77 carries 3 selah verses, oshb:Ps.77.4, oshb:Ps.77.10 and oshb:Ps.77.16 = web:Ps.77.3, web:Ps.77.9 and web:Ps.77.15 (unit = verses), so 'the psalm's third Selah' at web:Ps.77.15 is exact. The K/Q at oshb:Ps.77.12 is disclosed, the inline unpointed ketiv is genuinely present in the bytes ahead of the pointed qere (the hazard case), and the qere gloss agrees with both witnesses. Confidence 'medium' is honest calibration for a pivot the row itself concedes is arguable, and the rival it concedes is the right one. Two defects: the pivot's byte evidence omits the 1 word the pivot argument turns on, and device_notes carries an unanchored positional row reference. Observation: the back seam's stated close-warrant is selah plus content continuity, while the tier-1 driver actually sitting at that seam, 7 plural verb tokens with natural phenomena as subject across oshb:Ps.77.17-21 against 0 such tokens across oshb:Ps.77.14-16 (unit = tokens), is stated on neither side of the seam pair.

challenges.claim: The pivot verse's Hebrew quote covers the second half of the WEB clause it is said to match, leaving the 2 crux words the pivot reading depends on outside the byte evidence.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.77.11 = web:Ps.77.10 (shift+1) reads in full 'וָ֭אֹמַר חַלּ֣וֹתִי הִ֑יא שְׁ֝נ֗וֹת יְמִ֣ין עֶלְיֽוֹן'. The row quotes 'שְׁ֝נ֗וֹת יְמִ֣ין עֶלְיֽוֹן' (byte tier) and glosses the pair with “I will appeal to this: the years of the right hand of the Most High” (web:Ps.77.10). Those 3 Hebrew words correspond to the second half of that gloss; “I will appeal to this” (web:Ps.77.10) renders 'חַלּ֣וֹתִי הִ֑יא', 2 words that are absent from the row. The row calls web:Ps.77.10 the psalm's pivot and its structural crux, and the word carrying the disputed reading is the unquoted one, so quote and gloss fail to cover the same span at the point where the row's whole argument rests. The cure is a recut rather than a truncation of the English: carrying 2 more words from the same verse alongside the 3 already quoted restores parity at byte tier.

challenges.claim: device_notes points at 'the next row', an unanchored positional row reference where the standing rule requires cross-row reference to be verse-anchored.
challenges.evidence: The field reads 'redirects the whole composition from complaint toward the Exodus material of the next row'. The standing rule requires cross-row reference to be verse-anchored, and the anchor sits inside the same sentence's own material: the seam is web:Ps.77.15|web:Ps.77.16 = oshb:Ps.77.16|oshb:Ps.77.17, and the Exodus material pointed at runs 5 verses from the theophany at oshb:Ps.77.17 to 'בְּֽיַד מֹשֶׁ֥ה וְאַהֲרֹֽן' at oshb:Ps.77.21 = web:Ps.77.20. Verse-anchored, the sentence survives delivery of the row on its own; positionally, it breaks the moment the row is read singly or the order changes.

reviews.reasoning: Refs re-derived and correct; the range ref web:Ps.77.10-Ps.77.20 resolves to the rival span the rejected_alternative names and both its ends are valid WEB verses. The 2 Hebrew runs collate at byte tier. The span closes the psalm, and the cluster tiles web:Ps.77.1-20 exactly at 20 of 20 verses with no gap or overlap. The selah absence claim is properly span-scoped and true: 0 selah verses across oshb:Ps.77.17-21 (unit = verses), the psalm's 3 falling earlier. The intra-verse repetition claim here is better evidenced than its counterpart at the psalm's opening because both occurrences sit inside the quoted bytes, though its tier goes unnamed the same way: the 2 clauses in oshb:Ps.77.17 are byte False, accent_stripped True. I note that rather than file it, since a reader can see both of the 2 occurrences and check the tier. Three defects do stand: the stated seam driver misdescribes what sits on either side of the seam, the K/Q in the verse the sea-crossing motif is drawn from goes undisclosed, and the closing-frame universal ships without its sweep.

The latest first-person verbs sit back at oshb:Ps.77.13 = web:Ps.77.12 ('וְהָגִ֥יתִי' and 'אָשִֽׂיחָה'), 3 WEB verses before the seam; the verse immediately before the seam, oshb:Ps.77.16 = web:Ps.77.15, opens 'גָּאַ֣לְתָּ' and carries 'עַמֶּ֑ךָ', a second-person perfect with a second-person suffix rather than a first-person confessional verb. Second-person divine address is a byte-true device straddling this row's own seam, which argues continuity against the row unless disclosed, and the row does not disclose it. The same misreading reaches the close: 'the psalm closes on the narrative image itself' describes oshb:Ps.77.21 = web:Ps.77.20, which opens 'נָחִ֣יתָ' and carries 'עַמֶּ֑ךָ', 2 tokens of direct address rather than narrative. A replacement warrant that passes the test the original fails sits in-span: plural verbs with natural phenomena as subject run 7 tokens across oshb:Ps.77.17-21 against 0 tokens across oshb:Ps.77.14-16 (unit = tokens), which puts the register change at the seam without misdescribing either side of it.

challenges.claim: The row argues the sea-crossing motif from web:Ps.77.19 = oshb:Ps.77.20 and dual-cites that verse without disclosing its ketiv/qere, whose divergence falls inside the very clause the row's quote ellipsis skips.

The bytes at oshb:Ps.77.20 = web:Ps.77.19 carry the unpointed ketiv 'ושביליך' inline ahead of the pointed qere 'וּֽ֭שְׁבִֽילְךָ'; the ketiv holds a yod the qere does not, and WEB renders “your paths through the great waters” (web:Ps.77.19) as a plural. The row's quote is “Your way was through the sea… Your footsteps were not known” (web:Ps.77.19), whose ellipsis skips exactly the K/Q-bearing clause while the sentence around it argues 'the sea-crossing motif' from that verse. A quoted K/Q verse is disclosed when quoted; here the divergence is rendering-relevant as well, so the silence costs the reader the 1 fact needed to check the motif claim.
